transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I'm here because I've been struggling with these uncontrollable, repetitive thoughts that are starting to completely take over my daily life. I have this overwhelming fear of germs and contamination, which makes me feel like I constantly have to wash my hands and check things. It's just getting to be too much to handle on my own.
Can you tell me more about these repetitive behaviors, like washing your hands and checking things, and how often you feel compelled to do them?

I feel this overwhelming urge to wash my hands dozens of times a day just to get rid of any germs or contamination. I also constantly check things like my door locks and the stove switches over and over again to make sure everything is safe. I have to do these actions multiple times a day, and it has become incredibly exhausting.
How long have you been experiencing these obsessive thoughts and compulsive behaviors, and did they start suddenly or gradually over time?

I'm not entirely sure exactly how long I've been dealing with this, as it's hard to pinpoint a specific start date. I also can't really tell if it all started suddenly or if it just gradually got worse over time.
I'm not entirely sure how to describe the impact on my work or relationships specifically. They just take up so much of my time and energy every day that I feel constantly exhausted.
Have you ever experienced any sudden, repetitive movements or vocalizations, such as twitching or loud noises, in addition to your obsessive thoughts and compulsive behaviors?
No, I haven't ever experienced anything like that. I don't have any sudden, repetitive movements or vocalizations like twitching or making loud noises.
Are your obsessive thoughts limited to fears of germs and contamination, or do you experience obsessive thoughts about other things, such as order, symmetry, or harm coming to yourself or others?

No, it's not just germs; I also feel a strong urge for everything to be perfectly symmetrical and lined up. I constantly doubt if I've locked the doors or turned off appliances, and I even get highly distressing, intrusive thoughts about harming other people. It goes way beyond just worrying about contamination.
How distressing are these intrusive thoughts about harming others, and do you ever feel like you might act on them?

These thoughts are absolutely horrifying and cause me an immense amount of anxiety. I want to make it completely clear that I have absolutely no desire or intention to act on them, and the mere thought of actually hurting someone terrifies me.
How do you think these thoughts and behaviors are affecting your overall well-being, and what do you hope to achieve by seeking help for them?

It has been incredibly stressful and exhausting to deal with all of this. I'm not entirely sure how to describe the full impact on my well-being or what specific outcome to expect from seeking help. I just really want to find some relief from it all.
What are your expectations from the treatment, and are there any specific changes you hope to see in your symptoms or daily life as a result of seeking help for your OCD?

I'm not entirely sure yet what to expect from treatment, as this is all very new to me. I just really want to find some relief from these overwhelming thoughts and rituals so I can live a more normal daily life.

Are you willing to work with me to develop a treatment plan that may involve exposure to your fears and anxieties, as well as learning new ways to manage your thoughts and behaviors, in order to help you achieve your goal of finding relief from OCD symptoms?

I am definitely open to getting help and finding some relief from all of this. However, the idea of having to face my fears directly makes me feel really anxious and uncertain. I am willing to try if it will help me get better, even though it sounds very difficult.
